Then you use the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / 2a. You calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac) to see if you get two real roots, one real root, or complex ones. If the discriminant is positive, two real roots; if zero, one; if negative, complex.

To find the stationary points of y=f(x), you first take the derivative of f(x) and set it equal to zero. For example, if y = x³ - 3x², then f'(x) = 3x² - 6x. Setting this equal to zero gives 3x² - 6x = 0. Solving for x gives x = 0 and x = 2. Then, plug these values back into the original function to find the y-values. These are your stationary points. You can check if they're maxima or minima using the second derivative test.
